mainTopic: Leniency in the blessing כהן's comparisons, and the history and workings of the משמרות and מעמדות
overview: This amud opens by finishing a discussion about the כהן who recites ברכת כהנים. He is compared both to a נזיר and to a כהן serving in the מקדש. The comparisons are only an אסמכתא for rules מדרבנן, so they are used only to be lenient. The גמרא then turns to the משנה about the מעמדות. Because the daily קרבנות belong to all of ישראל, the נביאים set up twenty-four משמרות, and each one had a matching מעמד of כהנים, לוים and ישראלים. A ברייתא explains that half of each משמר lived in יריחו and supplied food and water. שמואל and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר disagree about who is required for the קרבן, depending on whether the לוים' song is mainly sung or played. The גמרא then traces how the משמרות grew to twenty-four, which is a מחלוקת תנאים about whether משה started with eight or sixteen. Finally, a ברייתא begins to tell how only four משמרות returned from בבל, and the story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Should a blemished כהן also be barred from blessing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes the comparison between the blessing כהן and the serving כהן one step further. Just as a serving כהן may not be a בעל מום, maybe a blessing כהן may not be one either.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then just as a כהן serving in the מקדש may not have a blemish, a כהן who blesses the people should also not be allowed to have a blemish!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison it has been using. If the blessing כהן is like the serving כהן, that should also bar a blemished כהן from blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the wine ban for the blessing כהן came from comparing him to a נזיר. The comparison to the serving כהן was brought to permit him grape pits, since a serving כהן may eat them. The challenge says this comparison should carry over fully, so the serving כהן's blemish rule should apply too.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן serving in the מקדש
A כהן reciting ברכת כהנים
A person with a physical blemish
"If just as... so too": a way of pushing a comparison further

phrases.aramaic: אִי מָה מְשָׁרֵת — בַּעַל מוּם לָא,
phrases.english: If so, just as a ministering priest — not one with a blemish,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּהֵן מְבָרֵךְ — בַּעַל מוּם לָא!
phrases.english: so too a priest who blesses — not one with a blemish!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה מְשָׁרֵת — בַּעַל מוּם לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier comparison of the blessing כהן to the serving כהן
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of the blessing כהן to the serving כהן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two are compared, every rule should carry over, including the blemish rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key question of how far a comparison drawn from פסוקים should be stretched.

steps.title: He is also compared to a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The blessing כהן is also compared to a נזיר, and a blemish does not matter for a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he is also compared to a נזיר, and a blemish does not disqualify a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is a second comparison, to a נזיר. That comparison points the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemish does not matter at all for a נזיר. Since the blessing כהן is compared to both, the נזיר comparison can cancel the blemish rule taken from the serving כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: He is compared (through a היקש, a link drawn from the פסוקים)
A person who took a vow to avoid wine and grape products

phrases.english: But he is juxtaposed to a nazirite.
phrases.notes: He means: a נזיר may have a blemish, so this comparison lets a blemished כהן bless.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a second comparison that blocks the first
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The serving-כהן comparison would bar a blemished כהן from blessing
steps.terutzMaskana: The נזיר comparison blocks that, so a blemish does not bar him

steps.title: Why use the comparisons leniently instead of strictly?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we choose the lenient side of each comparison. We could just as easily choose the strict side of each.
steps.simpleTranslation: What makes you use the comparisons to be lenient? Use them to be strict instead!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the way the two comparisons are being used. Each time, the lenient comparison wins; why not let the strict one win?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two comparisons could be combined in the strict direction. He would be like a נזיר and forbidden in grape pits. He would also be like a serving כהן and unfit when blemished. Nothing yet explains why leniency should be the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: "What did you see?": what makes you choose this side?
In the lenient direction
In the strict direction
Compare (draw the היקש)

phrases.english: And what did you see that you juxtapose for a leniency?
Juxtapose for a stringency!
phrases.notes: The strict way would be: like a נזיר he can't have grape pits, and like a serving כהן he can't have a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method used in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: Choosing the lenient side of each comparison
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both comparisons are equally valid, so there is no reason to prefer leniency over strictness.

steps.title: These are only supports for a rabbinic rule, so we are lenient
steps.stepSummary: The comparisons are only an אסמכתא for a rule that is מדרבנן. That is why we apply them leniently.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are only supports for rules that are מדרבנן, and so we apply them leniently.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that these rules are not truly from the תורה. The פסוקים are only a 'hook' for rabbinic rules, so we lean toward leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real תורה-level היקש would apply fully in both directions. Here the rule is מדרבנן, and the פסוקים are only an אסמכתא, a support. With a rabbinic rule we take the lenient path.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק used only as a support for a rule, not as its true source
From rabbinic law, not from the תורה itself

steps.whatToRemember: The comparisons of the blessing כהן to the serving כהן and to a נזיר are only an אסמכתא for rabbinic rules. So we use them only to be lenient.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the פסוקים here are the real source of a תורה law. The גמרא is saying they are only a support for a rabbinic rule.

phrases.english: They are supports for rabbinic law,
and therefore for leniency.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3 and closes the topic
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the status of the source (אסמכתא, not a true derivation)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparisons are full תורה-level links that could apply strictly
steps.terutzMaskana: They are only rabbinic supports, so we apply them leniently
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a general rule: when a rabbinic rule is only supported by a פסוק, we don't stretch the comparison to be strict.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about the מעמדות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to a new line of the משנה: 'These are the מעמדות, since it says צו את בני ישראל.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: These are the מעמדות, because it says: "Command the children of Israel..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. It is setting up a question about this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's wording is puzzling. It says 'these are the מעמדות' and then gives a פסוק as if it were a reason. The connection is not clear yet.

keyTerms.meaning: Groups of regular Jews (and כהנים and לוים) who stood for the people while the קרבנות were brought
"Since it is said": introduces a פסוק as a reason

phrases.english: These are the non-priestly watches.

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״צַו אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כּוּ׳״.
phrases.english: Since it is stated: "Command the children of Israel, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מעמדות are connected to the פסוק צו את בני ישראל

steps.title: What is the משנה saying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the משנה's line about the מעמדות fits together with the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the משנה saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the משנה's wording. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'these are the מעמדות' sounds like the start of a list. But then a פסוק comes right after it. The גמרא wants to know how the two parts connect.

keyTerms.meaning: "What is it saying?": a request to explain unclear wording

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording quoted in step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the line 'these are the מעמדות' connects to the פסוק

steps.title: The פסוק is the reason the מעמדות were set up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the משנה has two parts. First it names the topic, the מעמדות. Then it gives the reason for them, from the פסוק 'my offering, my food, for my fires'.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: These are the מעמדות. And why were the מעמדות set up? Because it says: "Command the children of Israel and say to them: My offering, My food, for My fires."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading an unspoken question into the משנה: 'Why were the מעמדות set up?' The פסוק is the answer to that question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'these are the מעמדות' are only a heading. The פסוק is the reason for them. It tells all of כלל ישראל to offer the daily קרבנות, so all of them need some connection to those offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: "This is what it means": introduces the correct reading
They set up (a rabbinic enactment)
"My offering, My food, for My fires": words from the פסוק

phrases.english: This is what it is saying: These are the non-priestly watches.
And what is the reason they instituted the non-priestly watches?
Since it is stated: "Command the children of Israel

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵיהֶם אֶת קׇרְבָּנִי לַחְמִי לְאִשַּׁי״.
phrases.english: and say to them: My offering, My food, for My fires."
phrases.notes: The point is that the command goes to all of בני ישראל, not just the כהנים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה means: these are the מעמדות, and the reason they were set up is the פסוק commanding all of Israel about the קרבנות

steps.title: How can a person's קרבן be brought without him there?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה raises a problem. The daily קרבנות belong to all of ישראל, but a person's קרבן shouldn't be brought while he is not standing by it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But how can a person's offering be brought while he is not standing next to it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues quoting the משנה. The משנה asks a question that sets up why the מעמדות were needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daily קרבנות are paid for by all of כלל ישראל, so they count as everyone's offering. Normally the owner of a קרבן should be present when it is brought. Of course, all of ישראל cannot stand in the מקדש every day.

keyTerms.meaning: How?
Standing by it (present at the offering)

phrases.english: And how can a person's offering be sacrificed
when he is not standing over it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the פסוק in step 7 to show why a fix was needed
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the people can be present at their own communal קרבנות

steps.title: The נביאים set up twenty-four משמרות with matching מעמדות
steps.stepSummary: The נביאים הראשונים set up twenty-four משמרות. Each one had a matching מעמד in ירושלים made up of כהנים, לוים and ישראלים. When it was a משמר's turn, its כהנים and לוים went up to ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The early prophets set up twenty-four משמרות. For every משמר there was a מעמד in ירושלים of כהנים, לוים and ישראלים. When the time came for a משמר to go up, the כהנים and לוים went up to ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its own question. It describes the system that lets representatives of the people stand by the קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהנים were split into twenty-four rotating groups, the משמרות. Each one was matched with a מעמד that included ישראלים, so regular Jews were represented at the offerings. The last line begins describing what happened when a group's turn came.

keyTerms.meaning: The early prophets
The rotating groups of כהנים who served in the מקדש
They established
To go up (to ירושלים)

steps.whatToRemember: The משמרות are the twenty-four groups of כהנים. Each one has a matching מעמד of כהנים, לוים and ישראלים, so the whole people is represented at the daily קרבנות.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up משמר and מעמד. The משמר is the group of כהנים doing the service. The מעמד is the matching group, including regular ישראלים, representing the people.

phrases.english: The early prophets instituted
twenty-four priestly watches.

phrases.aramaic: עַל כָּל מִשְׁמָר וּמִשְׁמָר הָיָה מַעֲמָד בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם
phrases.english: For each and every priestly watch there was a non-priestly watch in Jerusalem

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל כֹּהֲנִים וְשֶׁל לְוִיִּם וְשֶׁל יִשְׂרְאֵלִים.
phrases.english: of priests, of Levites, and of Israelites.
When the time arrived for a watch to ascend,
the priests and Levites would ascend to Jerusalem.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִתְקִינוּ נְבִיאִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה מִשְׁמָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The system of משמרות and matching מעמדות lets representatives of all ישראל stand by the קרבנות
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis of the whole מעמדות system that the rest of the משנה and גמרא go on to describe.

steps.title: A ברייתא: twenty-four משמרות in ארץ ישראל and twelve in יריחו
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says there were twenty-four משמרות in ארץ ישראל and twelve in יריחו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: There were twenty-four watches in ארץ ישראל, and twelve in יריחו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about where the משמרות lived. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the ברייתא seems to count two separate groups: twenty-four in ארץ ישראל plus twelve more in יריחו. The next step will point out that this reading cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught (opens a ברייתא)
Priestly watches, groups that took turns serving in the בית המקדש
Jericho, a city near ירושלים

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Twenty-four watches in Eretz Yisrael,
and twelve in Jericho.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds detail about the משמרות that the משנה described in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There were twenty-four משמרות in ארץ ישראל and twelve in יריחו.

steps.title: Twelve more in יריחו would be too many
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised: twelve extra in יריחו would make too many משמרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Twelve in יריחו?! That makes far too many!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the plain reading of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there were twenty-four in ארץ ישראל and twelve more in יריחו, that adds up to thirty-six משמרות. But we know there were only twenty-four, so the ברייתא can't mean that.

keyTerms.meaning: They are many, too many
A lot, very much

phrases.english: Twelve in Jericho?!
There are far too many of them!
phrases.notes: Twenty-four plus twelve makes thirty-six, but there were only twenty-four משמרות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement of twelve משמרות in יריחו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counting twelve in addition to twenty-four gives thirty-six, which is more than the known total.

steps.title: Twelve of the twenty-four were in יריחו
steps.stepSummary: The twelve in יריחו are part of the twenty-four. Half of each משמר came from יריחו to supply food and water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it as: twelve of them were in יריחו. When it was time for a watch to go up, half the watch went up from all over ארץ ישראל to ירושלים, and half went up from יריחו, so they could supply water and food to their brothers in ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא corrects the reading: the twelve in יריחו are counted inside the twenty-four, not on top of them. It then explains how this worked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each משמר was split in two. One half lived around ארץ ישראל and the other half lived in יריחו. The יריחו half helped by sending water and food to those serving in ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a corrected reading)
To go up (to ירושלים)
Food

phrases.english: Rather: twelve of them were in Jericho.
When the time came for the watch to go up,
half the watch would go up
from Eretz Yisrael to Jerusalem,
and half the watch would go up from Jericho,
so that they could supply water and food
to their brothers in Jerusalem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Twelve משמרות in יריחו in addition to the twenty-four.
steps.terutzMaskana: Twelve of the twenty-four were in יריחו. Half of each משמר came from יריחו to supply food and water.
steps.whatToRemember: There were only twenty-four משמרות. Half of each one lived in יריחו and sent food and water to ירושלים.

steps.title: שמואל: כהנים, לוים and ישראלים are required for the קרבן
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the קרבן cannot be brought without כהנים, לוים and ישראלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: כהנים, לוים and ישראלים are all required for the קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement about who must be present for the daily קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ties back to the מעמד from the משנה, which was made up of all three groups. According to שמואל, if any one of these groups is missing, the קרבן is held back.

keyTerms.meaning: Hold back, are required (without them it can't be done)
Regular Jews who are not כהנים or לוים

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Priests, Levites, and Israelites
are indispensable for the offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about who must be present for the קרבן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים, לוים and ישראלים are all required for the קרבן.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: כהנים, לוים and musical instruments
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: the required list is כהנים, לוים and כלי שיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: כהנים, לוים and musical instruments are required for the קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different opinion with a slightly different list. This sets up the question about what the two opinions disagree on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר swaps ישראלים for כלי שיר. So by him, the instruments themselves must be there, or the קרבן can't be brought.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
Musical instruments played by the לוים

phrases.aramaic: בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita that Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Priests, Levites, and musical instruments
are indispensable for the offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a contrasting list to שמואל's in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים, לוים and כלי שיר are required for the קרבן.

steps.title: What is their disagreement about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what idea lies behind the two different lists.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are they arguing about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the disagreement between שמואל and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants a basic principle that explains why one opinion lists ישראלים and the other lists instruments.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: With regard to what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what principle explains steps 13 and 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle behind the two lists

steps.title: Is the song mainly by voice or by instrument?
steps.stepSummary: שמואל holds the main part of the לוים' song is the voice. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds the main part is the instrument.
steps.simpleTranslation: One holds that the main part of the song is with the mouth. The other holds that the main part of the song is with an instrument.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the argument is about what counts as the real שירה of the לוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the song is mainly sung, the לוים are enough, and instruments are not required. If the song is mainly played, the instruments must be there too, so רבי שמעון בן אלעזר lists them.

keyTerms.meaning: One master holds
The main part of the song
With the mouth, by voice

phrases.english: One Sage holds: the main part of the song is vocal,
phrases.notes: This is שמואל, who did not list instruments.

phrases.english: and one Sage holds: the main part of the song is with an instrument.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue whether the main part of the לוים' song is vocal or instrumental.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: the song is mainly by voice, so instruments are not required. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: the song is mainly by instrument, so כלי שיר are required.

steps.title: משה made eight משמרות, שמואל sixteen, דוד twenty-four
steps.stepSummary: רב says the number of משמרות grew in stages: משה set eight, שמואל made sixteen, and דוד made twenty-four.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא בר גוריא said in the name of רב: משה set up eight משמרות for ישראל, four from אלעזר and four from איתמר. שמואל came and made them sixteen. דוד came and made them twenty-four, as it says: 'In the fortieth year of דוד's reign they were sought out, and among them were found mighty men of valor in יעזר גלעד.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement tracing the history of the משמרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רב, the משמרות grew in three separate stages, each by a different leader. The פסוק is brought to show that the final arrangement happened under דוד.

keyTerms.meaning: Set up, instituted
The two sons of אהרן from whom all כהנים come
Set them at (a number)

steps.confusionAlert: The שמואל here is שמואל הנביא, the prophet. He is not the אמורא שמואל from step 13.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: מֹשֶׁה תִּיקֵּן לָהֶם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל שְׁמוֹנָה מִשְׁמָרוֹת,
phrases.english: Moses instituted for the Jews eight watches,
four from Elazar and four from Itamar.

phrases.aramaic: בָּא שְׁמוּאֵל וְהֶעֱמִידָן עַל שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה,
phrases.english: Samuel came and set them at sixteen,

phrases.aramaic: בָּא דָּוִד וְהֶעֱמִידָן עַל עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה,
phrases.english: David came and set them at twenty-four,
as it is stated:
"In the fortieth year of the reign of David they were sought out,

phrases.aramaic: וַיִּמָּצֵא בָהֶם גִּבּוֹרֵי חַיִל בְּיַעְזֵיר גִּלְעָד״.
phrases.english: and there were found among them mighty men of valor at Jazer of Gilead."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the history of how the משמרות were set up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה set eight משמרות, שמואל made sixteen, and דוד made twenty-four.

steps.title: A ברייתא says דוד and שמואל made twenty-four together
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says דוד and שמואל together brought the number from eight to twenty-four. This seems to contradict רב's separate stages.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him from a ברייתא: משה set up eight משמרות for ישראל, four from אלעזר and four from איתמר. Then דוד and שמואל came and made them twenty-four, as it says: 'Whom דוד and שמואל the seer established in their trust.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב with a ברייתא that tells the story differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said שמואל went from eight to sixteen and דוד from sixteen to twenty-four. The ברייתא and its פסוק seem to say that דוד and שמואל did it together, in one step, from eight to twenty-four.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged (from a ברייתא)
Established, founded
The seer, a name for a נביא

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: מֹשֶׁה תִּיקֵּן לָהֶם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל שְׁמוֹנָה מִשְׁמָרוֹת,
phrases.english: Moses instituted for the Jews eight watches,
four from Elazar and four from Itamar,

phrases.aramaic: וּבָא דָּוִד וּשְׁמוּאֵל וְהֶעֱמִידָן עַל עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע,
phrases.english: and David and Samuel came and set them at twenty-four,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הֵמָּה יִסַּד דָּוִיד וּשְׁמוּאֵל הָרֹאֶה בֶּאֱמוּנָתָם״!
phrases.english: as it is stated: "Whom David and Samuel the seer established in their set office"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's statement in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that שמואל made sixteen and דוד made twenty-four separately
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא and the פסוק name דוד and שמואל together as setting up twenty-four, with no separate stage of sixteen.

steps.title: Building on what דוד and שמואל founded, it reached twenty-four
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means that the twenty-four grew out of the foundation laid by דוד and שמואל, step by step.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: from the foundation laid by דוד and שמואל of רמה, they set them at twenty-four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what the ברייתא really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not say that דוד and שמואל made twenty-four together at one time. It means the twenty-four came about through the work of both: שמואל's step to sixteen and דוד's step to twenty-four. So it fits with רב.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means
From the foundation of
From רמה, the hometown of שמואל הנביא

steps.whatToRemember: The משמרות grew in stages: משה made eight, שמואל made sixteen, and דוד made twenty-four. The ברייתא that names both of them together fits with this.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
From the foundation of David and Samuel of Rama
they set them at twenty-four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 by explaining the ברייתא so that it agrees with רב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: דוד and שמואל made twenty-four together, in one step.
steps.terutzMaskana: Through the work of both, in stages, the number reached twenty-four, just as רב said.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: משה set up sixteen watches
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא says משה set up sixteen משמרות, eight from אלעזר and eight from איתמר. When אלעזר's family grew, the total became twenty-four. It brings two פסוקים as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: משה set up sixteen משמרות for ישראל, eight from אלעזר and eight from איתמר. When the sons of אלעזר became more than the sons of איתמר, they divided them into twenty-four. The ברייתא proves this from two פסוקים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a different ברייתא with a different starting number: sixteen, not eight. This sets up the challenge against רב חמא בר גוריא that comes in step 23.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said משה set up eight משמרות. This ברייתא says משה already had sixteen. Only אלעזר's half doubled (8 to 16), while איתמר stayed at 8, which makes twenty-four.

keyTerms.meaning: Another ברייתא teaches
Priestly watches, groups of כהנים who took turns serving in the בית המקדש
The two sons of אהרן from whom all כהנים descend
A family branch
"And it says": introduces a second פסוק as extra proof

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:
Moshe set up for Israel
sixteen priestly watches,
eight from Elazar and eight from Itamar.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְשֶׁרַבּוּ בְּנֵי אֶלְעָזָר עַל בְּנֵי אִיתָמָר,
phrases.english: And when the sons of Elazar became more than the sons of Itamar,
they divided them and set them at twenty-four,
as it says: "And the sons of Elazar were found to be more
in chief men than the sons of Itamar,
and they divided them: for the sons of Elazar
sixteen heads of family branches,
and for the sons of Itamar, by their family branches, eight."
And it says:
"One family branch taken for Elazar,
and taken, taken for Itamar."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא with a different starting number from the one used in steps 17-19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה set up sixteen משמרות (8 + 8). אלעזר's side later grew to 16, making 24 in total.

steps.title: Why bring a second פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed to add the second פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the "and it says" add?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא added a second פסוק when the first one already seemed to prove its point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק gives the final numbers (16 and 8), but it does not say how they got there. The question pushes us to find what the second פסוק adds.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the point of

phrases.english: What is the "and it says" for?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the second proof-text quoted in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the second פסוק proves that the first did not.

steps.title: The second פסוק shows איתמר's side never grew
steps.stepSummary: Without the second פסוק, one might think איתמר also grew, from four to eight. The second פסוק shows that only אלעזר grew.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might say that just as the sons of אלעזר grew, the sons of איתמר also grew, and their eight were originally four. Come and hear: "One family branch taken for אלעזר, and taken, taken for איתמר."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the second פסוק blocks a mistaken reading: that both families grew from an original total of eight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading only the first פסוק, the starting point could have been 4 + 4 = 8, with both sides doubling. The second פסוק shows איתמר stayed the same. So the start must have been 8 + 8 = 16.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (a possible mistaken thought)
They increased, grew more numerous
Originally, at first
Come and hear: introduces a proof

phrases.english: And if you would say:
just as the sons of Elazar increased,
so too here the sons of Itamar increased,
and the eight were originally four,
come and hear:
"One family branch taken for Elazar,
and taken, taken for Itamar."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second פסוק shows that איתמר's eight stayed eight, so משה's original number was sixteen, not eight.

steps.title: This refutes רב חמא בר גוריא
steps.stepSummary: Since משה started with sixteen, the view that משה set up only eight seems disproven.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רב חמא בר גוריא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the ברייתא to strongly challenge רב חמא בר גוריא's teaching that משה set up only eight משמרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 claimed the stages were 8, then 16, then 24. This ברייתא says משה himself had sixteen, which directly contradicts that.

keyTerms.meaning: A strong refutation
The אמורא who reported the teaching of step 17

phrases.english: A refutation of Rav Ḥama bar Gurya!
phrases.notes: He taught in רב's name, back in step 17, that משה set up eight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the ברייתא of steps 20-22 into an attack on step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חמא בר גוריא's claim that משה set up eight משמרות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא proves from פסוקים that משה started with sixteen, so eight cannot be right.

steps.title: It is a מחלוקת between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא בר גוריא answers that the תנאים disagree, and he follows the תנא who said eight.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא בר גוריא can tell you: this is a מחלוקת between תנאים, and I spoke like the תנא who said eight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חמא בר גוריא by showing that his view has its own ברייתא behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא (step 18) said משה set up eight, and this ברייתא says sixteen. So the question is an open מחלוקת, and following one side is no mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a disagreement between תנאים
He could say to you

steps.whatToRemember: How many משמרות משה set up is a מחלוקת between תנאים: eight or sixteen. Either way, the final number was twenty-four.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְךָ רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥama bar Gurya can say to you:
It is a disagreement between תנאים,
and I said what I said
like the תנא who said eight.
phrases.notes: That is the ברייתא from step 18.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the two views are a מחלוקת between תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא of sixteen disproves רב חמא בר גוריא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ברייתא is one side of a מחלוקת, and רב חמא בר גוריא follows the side that says eight.

steps.title: Only four משמרות came back from the exile
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא teaches that only four משמרות came up from בבל: ידעיה, חרים, פשחור and אימר. It begins to tell what the נביאים among them did.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: four משמרות came up from the exile: ידעיה, חרים, פשחור and אימר. The נביאים among them arose...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא about the משמרות in the second בית המקדש. The sentence about the נביאים is not finished yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Out of twenty-four משמרות, only four returned from exile. This sets up a problem: how could twenty-four turns be filled? The rest of the ברייתא, which continues next, tells what the נביאים did about it.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught: introduces a ברייתא
Came up from the exile (back to ארץ ישראל)
Prophets

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Four priestly watches came up from the exile,
and these are they:
Jedaiah, Harim, Pashhur, and Immer.
The prophets among them arose,

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן אַרְבָּעָה מִשְׁמָרוֹת עָלוּ מִן הַגּוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how the משמרות began to what happened to them after the exile.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only four משמרות (ידעיה, חרים, פשחור, אימר) returned from בבל, and the נביאים among them took action.
